caption: Between the two of us we still argue about who forgot the furniture account had interest. Would you budget jointly with your partner?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R41 500
household income
Living in Sasolburg
slides.body:
Him 28, her 26
Married, no kids yet
Jobs: Sasol plant operator & Shoprite supervisor
Combined net: R41 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bed starter home, bought two years ago
slides.body: We got in before the rate hikes. I don't know how anyone starts now.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Boxer for basics, Spar for what Boxer doesn't stock
slides.body: Two trolleys, two different shops, every single month.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: One car between us, a 2021 Polo
slides.body: She drops me at the plant gate at five, then it's hers for the day.

slides.title: Petrol & insurance
slides.includes: The commute to the plant, comprehensive cover on one car
slides.body: Sasolburg isn't big, but shift work still empties a tank fast.

slides.title: Store account
slides.includes: The furniture account from when we moved in, eleven months left
slides.body: We financed a lounge suite and a fridge and I still wince at the interest.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, cellphone & fibre, retirement annuity, stokvel, funeral policy, gym, subscriptions
slides.body: None of these feels big alone. Add them up and it's nearly half of what we bring in.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R41 500 combined. We call it savings. Most months it becomes whatever breaks first.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded both our statements to Beyond Horizon and finally saw the household picture in one place.

The furniture account was worse than either of us admitted alone.

No bank login needed.
